doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Segregation and musicians
summary: Berry and Cooper say segregation was never the musicians' idea and describe police harassment.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I want to ask you another question about this. In a time when there wasn’t that much racial mixing, they say that at night after the bands got through, all the players would get together and jam anyhow because they all wanted to play together. Talk to us about how the music made a bridge there.
Well that business of segregation was never the musicians’ idea. You know this is the one thing where you didn’t have that happening. Although it was illegal in some places, literally illegal.

If you’re on the wrong side of town, or anytime at that time night or day and you saw the cops, they’d say hey, what you doing in this district vice versa you know. But anyway, they always find a way to merge. It never fails in I mean musicians. I mean it’s not that ethnic in there, you know, believe me. You understand what I’m saying? It’s not there, and never has been, not among musicians, not in my experience.
